Wizard_Language.T: SelfX package wizard

This wizard asks a few questions, writes your settings into a copy of the package and builds the Intune package. Your repository files are not changed. Press Enter to accept the value in brackets. Every question has a recommendation.

Default language of SelfX on the devices (de, en, fr, es ... or Auto)
Auto follows the display language of Windows. Choose Auto if your users speak several languages.
May users choose their language in the settings?
Yes. It costs nothing and helps multilingual staff.
Name of your organisation (used for the Intune app name and the instructions)
The short name of your company or authority, for example Contoso.
Name of the tool in the title bar and the shortcuts
Keep SelfX. Users find it faster when the name is the same everywhere.
Support e-mail address (shared mailbox)
Use a shared (functional) mailbox, never a personal one. The address is also the recipient of the device logs e-mail.
Support phone number (empty = hide)
Enter a number only if somebody answers it during the support hours.
Support hours (empty = hide)
For example Mon-Fri 08:00-17:00.
Support website or ticket portal (https://, empty = hide)
Enter your self-service portal if you have one. Only https:// addresses are accepted.
Teams contact (address of a shared account or https:// link, empty = hide)
Optional. Leave it empty if the Service Desk is not reachable in Teams.
Path of your logo file (png, jpg, ico, bmp or gif, empty = no logo)
A transparent PNG, about 400 x 120 pixels, looks good in the light and the dark design.
Company color as #RRGGBB (empty = keep SelfX blue #0072BC)
Use your corporate color. SelfX adjusts colors that are too dark or too light.
Do you want the ticket function (the user describes the problem, SelfX opens a prepared e-mail)?
Yes, if your Service Desk accepts tickets by e-mail. The user always checks and sends the e-mail; SelfX sends nothing itself.
Default recipient of ticket e-mails
Your Service Desk mailbox. It is used when no organisation rule matches.
Marker at the start of the subject line (for mail filters)
Keep SelfX, or use a short tag your ticket system filters on. Up to 20 characters: letters, digits . _ -
Do tickets of other organisations or locations have to go to other mailboxes?
Answer yes if several IT units are responsible for different devices. You then define one unit per mailbox.
Are devices hybrid joined (Active Directory)? Then SelfX can route by OU.
Yes, if your devices are in an on-premises domain. Cloud-only (Entra joined) devices have no OU.
Do you route by the Autopilot group tag (Entra ID)?
Yes, if your Autopilot devices carry a group tag per organisation. It is the most reliable criterion for cloud-only devices.
Do you route by device class (notebook, PC, tablet)?
Yes, if another team handles tablets or kiosk PCs. SelfX runs on Windows 11 only: smartphones (iOS, Android) cannot be covered by SelfX.
Organisation / unit {0}
Short name of the unit (letters, digits . _ -)
For example IT-Berlin. The name is only used inside the configuration.
Mailbox of this unit
One plain address, shared mailbox only. The file Ticket_Config.xml can be read by every user on the device. Addresses that must stay hidden belong into the per-device registry value TicketMail.
Copy (Cc) of this unit (empty = none)
Optional second shared mailbox.
Autopilot group tags of this unit (comma separated)
Exactly as in Entra ID, for example DE-IT1-BER. Letters, digits, space . _ - up to 64 characters.
OU names of this unit (comma separated)
Part of the distinguished name, for example OU=Berlin. SelfX searches it in the OU of the computer account.
Device classes of this unit (comma separated)
Free names such as Notebook, Desktop, Tablet. Intune sets the value per device group.
Add another unit?
Yes until every mailbox is defined. The first matching rule wins: group tags are checked first, then OUs, then device classes.
Do you have Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat licensed and want to offer it in the help dialog?
Yes if your users have Copilot Chat. SelfX uses no interface and no token: it prepares a text, the user pastes it into Copilot.
Do you want a button that opens the wiki or intranet page of your company in the web browser?
Yes if you have a wiki with tips and tricks for your staff. The button is shown in the navigation of SelfX.
Address of the wiki (https://)
The page that opens on a click, for example https://wiki.contoso.example. Only https:// is accepted.
Name on the button (empty = Company wiki, up to 40 characters)
Optional, for example Contoso Wiki. Empty shows a text in the language of the user.
Who is the answer for? User (plain language) or Admin (technical steps)
User. Technical answers confuse most employees.
Empty the clipboard a few minutes after SelfX copied the text?
Yes if the text should not stay in the clipboard. The text already contains no names or addresses.
Show the status icon next to the clock for all users?
Yes. Users see problems early and open SelfX with one click.
Create a shortcut on the public desktop?
Yes for the start, so that users find SelfX. Switch it off later if desktops should stay empty.
Create a shortcut in the Start menu?
Yes.
Do you want to change security and log settings (expert)?
No. The secure defaults stay: the service starts nothing when files do not match (Enforce) and runs with reduced rights (Restricted).
Days to keep log files (1-3650)
90 days is a good balance between support needs and data minimisation.
File check of the service: Enforce or Audit
Enforce. Audit only reports and is meant for a short pilot.
Rights of the service: Restricted or Default
Restricted. Default is only for troubleshooting.
Path of IntuneWinAppUtil.exe (Win32 Content Prep Tool of Microsoft)
Download it from https://github.com/microsoft/Microsoft-Win32-Content-Prep-Tool (file IntuneWinAppUtil.exe in the repository, use the latest release tag). The script checks the Microsoft signature.
The programs (folder Bin) are missing or outdated. Build them now with the .NET SDK 10?
Yes. The build needs the .NET SDK 10 but no internet: the packages come from the folder offline-feed.
Output folder
The folder receives the package, the detection script, the scripts for Intune and the instructions. Do not commit it.
Summary of your answers
Create the package with these settings?
Yes, if the summary is correct. Nothing is installed or sent; the package is only built.

SelfX in Intune: short instructions for {0} (version {1})
Open the Microsoft Intune admin center (intune.microsoft.com). Always start with a small pilot group.
1. Create the app: Apps > Windows > Add > Windows app (Win32). Upload {0}. Name: {1}. Publisher: {2}.
2. Program: install command: {0}
Uninstall command: {0}
Install behavior: System. Device restart behavior: no specific action.

3. Requirements: 64-bit, Windows 11 25H2 (build 26200 or newer). If the portal does not offer 25H2, add a script requirement: integer, greater than or equal to 26200, script: [int](Get-ItemPropertyValue -Path 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion' -Name CurrentBuildNumber)
4. Detection rule: custom script. Upload {0} (not the file in the repository). Run script as 32-bit process: No. Enforce script signature check: No.
5. Dependency: PowerShell 7.6 or newer as its own Win32 app (MSI of Microsoft), Automatically install: Yes. Details: docs\Installation.md, chapter 3.2.
6. Assignment: assign the app as Required to a pilot device group. Do not add SelfX or PowerShell 7 to the blocking apps of the Autopilot status page (ESP).

7. Ticket routing: create one platform script per file below (Devices > Scripts and remediations > Platform scripts). Run this script using the logged on credentials: No. Run script in 64-bit PowerShell: Yes. Assign each script to the matching Entra device group; the groups should exclude each other.
{0}: group tags {1}; device classes {2}
Tip for a dynamic device group of a group tag: (device.devicePhysicalIds -any (_ -eq "[OrderID]:TAG"))
{0}. Test on a pilot device: the Start menu shows SelfX, the service SelfXService runs, the logs are in %ProgramData%\SelfX\Logs. Then widen the assignment.
